# Creational Pattern: Factory Pattern

In Factory pattern, we create the object of the class without exposing the creation/instantiation logic to the user who wants to create the object and then return the newly created object using a common interface which is inherited by the class.

Example:

![Embedded image](data:image/png;base64,)

The VehicleFactory.cs class looks like below:

![Embedded image](data:image/png;base64,)

We see that we pass the information about the object to the VehicleFactory.

But the problem is that let’s say we want to add Truck class; so in the VehicleFactory we change the code to add some new Condition which is sometimes a bad situation, so that’s why we are able to say that “they violate the Open-Close Principle”.
